title: Should Governments Put A Tax On Meat?

contexts.text: Governments deciding now whether to put a tax on meat. The thesis names no country and no time, so the decision is any government's that would enact the tax. A claim about another country's or another policy's experience (an analogy's source case, a study) is evidence about this decision: an instance in this context whose formulas name that case.

actors.text: The governments that would put the tax on meat: the thesis's agent, the one who acts in a policy debate (guidelines §3, OC13). The people the tax affects are others, even when an action's phrase names them.

status: Drafted by Claude Code on 2026-11-24 from the thesis, the lexicon and the gold: the actions the discussion deliberates or proposes, each the governments'. What people would do in response (switching to other protein, buying iron supplements) is a consequence, a state, not a declared action. Not verified by a person (D045).
